edges.description: COQ2 catalyses an obligate step, so reduced activity reduces CoQ10 output.
Coenzyme Q is the carrier between complexes I/II and complex III, so its depletion interrupts the chain at that point.
Reduced ubiquinol is the principal lipid-phase antioxidant of the inner mitochondrial membrane, and is lost along with the carrier function.

Photoreceptors and retinal ganglion cells are high-oxidative-demand tissues, so the retinal branch is placed downstream of the same upstream failures as the podocyte and neuronal branches. The intermediates are unknown because no retinal-tissue study exists in this disease; the link is inferred rather than measured, which is why it is drawn as an indirect edge with unknown intermediates rather than a direct one.

edges.description: Reads out residual catalytic activity of a human allele in a null yeast background, as a quantitative surrogate for enzyme function.
edges.limitations: Yeast CoQ biosynthesis and membrane composition differ from human, and the readout is growth-based complementation rather than direct measurement of human tissue CoQ. It cannot capture tissue-specific residual activity, which is precisely what would explain why one organ is affected and another is spared in the same patient.

edges.description: Develops mitochondrial encephalopathy, which is the human manifestation that CoQ10 fails to treat — so the model reproduces precisely the arm of the disease that needed a model.
edges.limitations: The modelled allele is a mouse Coq2 variant, not one of the human alleles catalogued in the yeast series, and mouse CoQ9/CoQ10 proportions differ from human, which is one of the stated reasons exogenous CoQ10 behaves differently across species. Renal phenotype is not the focus.

nodes.description:
An experimental substrate-enhancement strategy. 4-HBA is the natural substrate of COQ2, and raising its availability is proposed to compensate for defective substrate delivery and drive residual enzyme activity, restoring endogenous rather than supplying exogenous CoQ. In a mouse carrying the Coq2A252V variant, lifelong 4-HBA prevented mitochondrial encephalopathy where conventional CoQ10 did not, and withdrawal caused progressive neurological decline.
On the strength of that, a first-in-human individual therapeutic trial was started in a 3-year-old boy with biallelic COQ2 variants and a Leigh-like syndrome who had responded minimally to high-dose CoQ10. Over six months he had sustained remission of proteinuria, rising serum CoQ10, and gains in motor, language and cognitive development, with no adverse effects. This is one patient over six months and the authors say further clinical investigation is needed; it is curated because it is the first therapy directed at the arm of the disease CoQ10 cannot reach.

evidence.reference_title: Preclinical and first-in-human evidence of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid for mitochondrial COQ2 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that lifelong 4-HBA supplementation in a murine model carrying the pathogenic Coq2A252V variant is well tolerated and prevents the onset of mitochondrial encephalopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Preclinical and first-in-human evidence of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid for mitochondrial COQ2 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Following the initiation of oral 4-HBA treatment, the patient experienced rapid and sustained remission of proteinuria, improved renal hyperfiltration and a gradual increase in serum CoQ10 concentrations.

nodes.description: Ataxia belongs to the intermediate childhood-onset phenotype. Note that an ataxic form with cerebellar atrophy was one of the three phenotypes recognised for primary CoQ10 deficiency as a group before the genes were known; for COQ2 specifically the ataxia sits within the childhood-onset presentation.

evidence.snippet: an intermediate childhood-onset phenotype characterized by developmental delay, ataxia, muscular hypotonia, and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome progressing to neurodegeneration and kidney failure

nodes.description: Biallelic COQ2 variants reduce the activity of the mitochondrial polyprenyltransferase that condenses 4-hydroxybenzoate with the polyisoprenoid tail. The protein localises to mitochondria with its C-terminus facing the intermembrane space. Residual activity is not all-or-nothing: yeast complementation across the reported allelic series grades each mutant, and that grade predicts the patient's phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: The COQ2 genotype predicts the severity of coenzyme Q10 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Our findings show that the main functional transcript of COQ2 is shorter than what was previously reported and that its protein product localizes to mitochondria with the C-terminus facing the intermembrane space.

nodes.description: Progressive retinal dystrophy with cone dysfunction exceeding rod dysfunction, confirmed on electroretinography, with a bull's eye pattern of pigmentary change and ellipsoid-zone loss on optical coherence tomography. Reported in a child with biallelic COQ2 variants whose visual acuity fell from 20/40 to 20/400 in the worse eye over roughly two and a half years. Retinopathy in primary CoQ10 deficiency has been reported only with COQ2 variants.

nodes.description: Reduced coenzyme Q (ubiquinol) is the main lipid-soluble antioxidant of mitochondrial membranes, so primary CoQ deficiency removes antioxidant protection at the same time and in the same compartment as it removes electron transfer. This node is curated separately from the bioenergetic one because the two are distinct claims and a therapy could in principle restore one without the other; no study in COQ2 patients has separated them.

Encephalopathy, developmental delay, ataxia, hypotonia and intractable seizures. The critical property of this node is that it does not respond to oral CoQ10: the neurological arm of the disease continues to progress in patients whose renal and metabolic manifestations have remitted on treatment. The proposed reason is pharmacokinetic rather than mechanistic — CoQ10 is very lipophilic and crosses the blood-brain barrier poorly.

nodes.description:
High-dose oral CoQ10 is the standard treatment. In a 116-patient international series with a median two years of follow-up it reduced proteinuria by 88% at 12 months and improved five-year kidney failure-free survival from 19% to 62%, with uncommon and mild side effects. The authors conclude that every patient diagnosed with primary CoQ10 deficiency should receive early lifelong supplementation.
The limitation is as well established as the benefit: it does not rescue established neurological disease, even when started on the first day of life.

evidence.reference_title: Oral Coenzyme Q10 supplementation leads to better preservation of kidney function in steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome due to primary Coenzyme Q10 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: CoQ10 supplementation led to significantly better preservation of kidney function (5-year kidney failure-free survival 62% vs. 19%) with an improvement in general condition and neurological manifestations.

evidence.reference_title: Oral Coenzyme Q10 supplementation leads to better preservation of kidney function in steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome due to primary Coenzyme Q10 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: our findings indicate that all patients diagnosed with primary CoQ10 deficiency should receive early and life-long CoQ10 supplementation to decelerate the progression of kidney disease and prevent further damage to other organs.

evidence.reference_title: COQ2-Associated Primary Coenzyme Q10 Deficiency Presenting With Proteinuria: A Case Report and Literature Review.
evidence.snippet: After oral administration of high-dose CoQ10 (85 mg/kg/d) combined with enalapril maleate (0.80 mL/kg/d), the patient achieved complete remission of proteinuria and maintained stable renal function.

evidence.reference_title: COQ2-Associated Primary Coenzyme Q10 Deficiency Presenting With Proteinuria: A Case Report and Literature Review.
evidence.snippet: the therapeutic outcomes suggest that all diagnosed patients require long-term supplementation with adequate doses of CoQ10, which is of great significance for delaying disease progression

nodes.description: The glomerular podocyte is the kidney cell that fails. It is terminally differentiated, mitochondria-rich and cannot be replaced, which is the standard explanation for why CoQ biosynthesis defects present as steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome rather than as a tubulopathy. Kidney involvement is the hallmark manifestation of the nephropathic CoQ deficiencies, and in COQ2 it is often the presenting problem.

evidence.reference_title: Oral Coenzyme Q10 supplementation leads to better preservation of kidney function in steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome due to primary Coenzyme Q10 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Primary Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) deficiency is an ultra-rare disorder caused by defects in genes involved in CoQ10 biosynthesis leading to multidrug-resistant nephrotic syndrome as the hallmark kidney manifestation.

evidence.reference_title: Response to Early Coenzyme Q10 Supplementation Is not Sustained in CoQ10 Deficiency Caused by CoQ2 Mutation.
evidence.snippet: Index cases from two families presented with vomiting, nephrotic range proteinuria, and diabetes in early infancy.

nodes.description: Progressive loss of kidney function. Half of COQ2 patients reached kidney failure by age five without treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Variation of the clinical spectrum and genotype-phenotype associations in Coenzyme Q10 deficiency associated glomerulopathy.
evidence.snippet: At adult age, kidney survival was equally poor (20-25%) across all disorders.

nodes.description: Without sufficient coenzyme Q, electrons cannot pass from complexes I and II to complex III, so oxidative phosphorylation is impaired and lactate accumulates. This is the node that the two therapeutic strategies — exogenous CoQ10 and 4-HBA substrate enhancement — both aim at, by different routes.

evidence.reference_title: Preclinical and first-in-human evidence of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid for mitochondrial COQ2 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Coenzyme Q (CoQ) is a key component of the mitochondrial respiratory chain and is essential for cellular energy production and metabolic homeostasis.

nodes.description:
Photoreceptors and retinal ganglion cell axons are among the most energy-demanding tissues in the body, and they fail in COQ2 disease with a cone-greater-than-rod pattern on electroretinography plus optic nerve atrophy. This node matters out of proportion to its frequency because retinopathy in primary CoQ10 deficiency has been reported only with COQ2 variants, which makes it the most gene-discriminating feature of the entry.
Unlike the podocyte and neuronal nodes, no retinal-tissue study exists. The mechanism here is inferred from the shared respiratory-chain lesion upstream and from the ophthalmological phenotyping of genotyped patients, not demonstrated in retina, so the node asserts the site of failure and not a retina-specific pathway.

In roughly a third of COQ2 patients kidney involvement is isolated at diagnosis, so a child can reach a nephrologist with no reason to suspect a mitochondrial disease.

nodes.description: Reported in four patients from two families presenting with neonatal diabetes and nephrotic-range proteinuria; the renal and endocrine features responded to CoQ10 and the neurological course did not.
The founding allele, homozygous in two siblings with the infantile form. It changes a highly conserved tyrosine within a predicted transmembrane domain.
